content.comment_body: I have a [company_name] [product_name], and I’m unsure how to access the data logging stored on its SD card. How can I view or download the registration data (.csv) from the SD card to my PC using Ethernet? Is it possible to access the recorded data through the SD card using [product_name] [product_name] software? Thank you.

Have you tried this with your device? I only use [product_name] [product_name] for programming and transferring software, but recently needed to download logged data. 1- If the SD card has stored data over several hours or days, I can download it to my PC using [product_name] [product_name] software, provided the number of lines does not exceed 20,000, and no new .csv file has been created. Otherwise, I have to remove the SD card and copy the files with a card reader. 2- After downloading, does the old data on the SD card get deleted or does it stay? Thanks again.

When reading data from the SD card, the [product_name] software does not delete the information. In the current .csv file, there may be time gaps because no data is written during the readout. If a log file becomes full, the [product_name] creates a new .csv file on the SD card, provided there is enough space.

analysis.insight_summary: Users want to know how to access and download logging files from the SD card of their [product_name] device using [product_name] [product_name] software via Ethernet. They have questions about limitations on file size, how new files are created, and whether data is deleted or modified after downloading. There is confusion around file management and the need for SD card removal when files exceed certain parameters.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to conveniently manage and retrieve history and logging data from their device's SD card using the supplied software over Ethernet, ideally without having to physically remove the SD card.
